children.translated_text: I shall set forth a collection of prescribed single-meaning, multiple-meaning, and regional words,
the Nighaṇṭuśeṣa, after bowing to the lotus feet of the Arhat.
Kapītana, karṇapūra, bhaṇḍila, and śyāmavalkala are also names in this group.
For pāṭalī: pāṭalā, sthālī, moghā, and toyādhivāsinī.
Also dūtī of spring and love, kuntī, and kālavṛntikā.

children.text: anyasyāṃ tatra tu śvetā pāṭalā kāṣṭhapāṭalā
children.translated_text: For another tree in that class: śvetā, pāṭalā, and kāṣṭhapāṭalā.
Śītalā, śvetakumbhīkā, kuberākṣī, and phaleruhā are also names.
For aguru: agaru, loha, vaṃśika, and viśvarūpaka.
Kṛmija, pravara, rājārha, yogaja, and anāryaka are also names for it.
For malligandha, the name here is maṅgalyā; for the black variety, kākatuṇḍaka.
For śrīkhaṇḍa: malayaja, candana, and śvetacandana.
Gośīrṣaka, gandhasāra, bhadraśrī, and tailaparṇika are also names.
Phalakī, surabhi, sāra, mahārha, and rohaṇodbhava are further names.
Next, for barbaraka: śveta, nirgandha, and barbarodbhava.
For red sandalwood: kṣudracandana and bhāskarapriya.
Tāmrasāra, raktasāra, lohita, and haricandana are also names.
For kucandana: pattrāṅga, pattaṅga, and paṭṭarañjana.
Suraṅgaka, raktakāṣṭha, pattūra, and tilaparṇikā are also names.
Next: drumotpala, vyādha, parivyādha, and sugandhaka.
For this scentless tree: karṇikāra, niṣīdha, and pītapuṣpaka.
For puṃnāga: mahānāga, kesara, and raktakesara.
Devavallabha, kumbhīka, tuṅga, and puruṣanāmaka are also names.
Next, for agasti: vaṅgasena, śukanāsa, and munidruma.
For karavīra: kaṇavīra, śvetapuṣpa, and aśvamāraka.
Pratihāsa, śataprāśa, aśvarodha, and kumudodbhava are also names.
For its red-flowered variety: laguḍa, caṇḍāta, and caṇḍagulmaka.
For tamāla: kālaskandha, tāpiccha, rañjata, and vasu.
For tamāla leaf: vastrākhya, romaśa, tāmasa, and dala.
For small cardamom: candrabālā, drāviḍī, niṣkuṭi, and truṭi.
Kapotavarṇikā, tucchā, koraṅgī, bahulā, and tulā are also names.
For large cardamom: bṛhadelā, bhadrailā, and tvaksugandhikā.

children.text: tridivodbhavā ca pṛthvīkā karṇikā tripuṭā puṭā
children.translated_text: Tridivodbhavā, pṛthvīkā, karṇikā, tripuṭā, and puṭā are also names.
For camphor: ghanasāra, himāhva, and himavāluka.
Sitābhra, śītalaraja, sphaṭika, and candranāmaka are also names.
For kaṅkolaka: kaṭuphala, komaka, and māgadhotthita.
Kola, koṣaphala, kora, marīca, and dvīpa are also given as names.

children.text: lavaṅge śiṣaraṃ divyaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ vārijaṃ lavam ||
children.translated_text: For clove: śiśira, divya, bhṛṅgāra, vārija, and lava.
Śrīpuṣpa, śryāhvaya, devapuṣpa, and candanapuṣpaka are also names.
For nalikā: kapotāṅghri, nirmadhyā, śuṣirā, and naṭī.
Dhamanī, añjanakeśī, śūnyā, and vidrumavallī are also names.
For atimukta: maṇḍaka, puṇḍraka, and bhramarotsava.
Parāśraya, suvāsantī, kāmuka, and mādhavī-latā are also names.
For pippala: bodhi, aśvattha, śrīvṛkṣa, and calapattraka.
Maṅgalya, keśavāvāsa, śyāmala, and dviradāśana are also names.
For gardabhāṇḍa: kandarāla, chāyāvṛkṣa, and kamaṇḍalu.
Plakṣa, vaṭaplava, śuṅgī, supārśva, and cārudarśana are also names.
For kapītana: kapīna, pītana, and plavaka.

children.text: karpaṭaḥ parkaṭī plakṣaḥ satīdo lakṣaṇe naṭī
children.translated_text: Karpaṭa, parkaṭī, plakṣa, satīda, and naṭī are given under lakṣaṇa.
For vaṭa: vaiśravaṇāvāsa, nyagrodha, bahupād, and dhruva.
Skandhajanman, raktaphala, kṣīrin, śuṅgī, and vanaspati are also names.
For udumbara: jantuphala, yajñāṅga, and hemadugdhaka.
Sadāphala, vasuvṛkṣa, śvetavalka, and maśaka are also names.
Phalārājī, phalabhārī, phalayū, and jaghanephalā are also names.
For rājādana: rājanyā, kṣīrikā, and priyadarśana.
Kapipriya, dṛḍhaskandha, madhurājaphala, and nṛpa are also names.
For piyāla: rājavṛkṣa, bahuvalka, and dhanuṣpaṭa.
Sannakadru, kharaskandha, cāra, and tāpasavallabha are also names.
For āmrātaka: varṣapākī, kapicūta, and kapipriya.
Kapītana, pītanaka, tanukṣīra, and amrapāṭaka are also names.
For rājārka: kṣīrārkaparṇa; for alarka: gaṇarūpaka.
Ekāṣṭhīla, sadāpuṣpa, mandāra, and pratāpasa are also names.
For truṭi: vajra, mahāvṛkṣa, asipatra, sruk, sudhā, and guḍā.
Samantadugdhā, sehuṇḍa, śaṇḍerī, and cakrakaṇṭaka are also names.
For karamarda: karamada, karāmraka, and suṣeṇaka.
Sthalaparkeṭa, āvigna, and kṛṣṇapākaphala are also names.
For jambīra: jambhala, jambha, jambhīla, and dantaharṣaṇa.
Vaktraśodhin, dantaśaṭha, gambhīra, and rocana are also names.
For karuṇa: chāgalākhya, mallikākusuma, and priya.
For bījapūra: bījapūrṇa, pūraka, and phalapūraka.
Supūraka, mātuluṅga, kesarāmla, and amlakesara are also names.
Varāmla, bījaka, luṅga, rucaka, and madhyakesara are also names.
Kṛmighna, gandhakusuma, kesarī, and sādhupādapa are also names.
For mātuluṅgī: vardhamānā, madhurā, and madhukarkaṭī.
Madhuvallī, pūtipuṣpā, devadūtī, and mahābalā are also names.
For amlikā: cukrikāmlā, śuktikāmlī, and vikāmlikā.
Cukrā, ciñcā, tintiḍīkā, tintiḍī, and gurupuṣpikā are also names.
That same plant is <s>śaṅkhadrāvaka</s>, inferior, and <s>lauhadrāvaka</s>, excellent.
Those two respectively are called <s>śatavedhin</s> and <s>sahasravedhin</s>.

children.text: site tu tatra kadaraḥ kārmakaḥ kubjakaṇṭakaḥ
children.translated_text: For the white variety of it: <s>kadara</s>, <s>kārmaka</s>, and <s>kubjakaṇṭaka</s> are used.

children.text: kaṇṭakāḍhyā nalaphalī picchā tu tasya veṣṭakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakāḍhyā</s> and <s>nalaphalī</s> are names; its enclosing sheath is called <s>picchā</s>.
For the inferior <s>śālmalī</s>, <s>rocana</s> and <s>kūṭaśālmali</s> are stated.
<s>Kṛṣṇasārā</s>, <s>aṅgāravarṇā</s>, and <s>aguru</s> are names; the small one is <s>śiṃśipā</s>.

children.text: maṅgalyā śucipattrā ca phale tasyāstu sāṅgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅgalyā</s> and <s>śucipattrā</s> are also names; its fruit is <s>sāṅgara</s>.

children.text: guggulau tu puro durgo mahiṣākṣaḥ palaṅkaṣaḥ
parvakāḍhyā tiṣyaphalā mākandī śrīphalā ca sā ||
aralau dundako dīrgha vṛntaś cātha kuṭannaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>aralu</s>: <s>dundaka</s> and <s>dīrghavṛnta</s> are used; next comes <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>.
Of this, the white variety is <s>śvetamarica</s>, while the red one is <s>madhuśigruka</s>.

children.text: kulāvo nandinaścāpi sitaḥ kṛṣṇaśca sa dvidhā
children.translated_text: <s>Kulāva</s> and <s>nandin</s> are also names; it is of two kinds, white and black.

children.text: sa tu dvidhā śikhigrīvaḥ śreṣṭho gomūtragandhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That one is of two kinds: <s>śikhigrīva</s> is the best, and <s>gomūtragandhaka</s> is another.

children.text: śāke kolaphalo dvā dārur yogī halīmakaḥ
sillake tu siddhavṛkṣaḥ kolipattre tu joraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>sillaka</s> there is <s>siddhavṛkṣa</s>; for <s>kolipattra</s> there is <s>joraṇa</s>.
For <s>mahāpattra</s>, beginning with the bark, there is <s>viṣaśaṅku</s> and <s>palāśaka</s>.

children.text: dāru vasnehaviddaṃ ca devadruḥ svargajo drumaḥ ||

children.translated_text: <s>Madhūka</s> and <s>śāka</s> are names; so too <s>mādhava</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>madhu</s>.
For this water-born one, <s>madhūla</s> is used; for the mountain-born kind, <s>dīrghapattraka</s>.
Also <s>tīravṛkṣa</s>, <s>gauraśāla</s>, and the one with short flowers and fruit.

children.text: rodhre lodhraḥ site tatra śābaras tanuvalkalaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>rodhra</s>: <s>lodhra</s>; in its white variety, <s>śābara</s> and <s>tanuvalkala</s>.

children.text: rakte tu paṭṭikā tilvaḥ paṭṭī lākṣāprasādanaḥ

children.translated_text: This spring tree is <s>sahakāra</s> when it is especially fragrant.
<s>Ṭaṅka</s> and <s>nīlakapittha</s> are another kind; <s>rājaputra</s> and <s>nṛpātmaja</s> are names.
Ariṣṭa, hiṅguniryāsa, vetā, and niyamana are also names.
For mahānimba: nimbaka, kārmuka, and viṣamuṣṭika.
Ramyaka, kṣībaka, vṛkṣa, akṣipīlu, and keśamuṣṭika are also names.
For pīlu: sraṃsī, sahasrāṅga, śīta, and karabhavallabha.
Gulmāri and guḍaphala are also names; now, for the mountain-born one:
Akṣoṭa, karparāla, phalasneha, and guhāśaya are names.
For pārāvāta: sārāmla, raktamāla, and parāvata.
Ārevata, sāraphala, mahāpārāvata, and mahān are also names.
For rudrākṣa, whose fruit is like a pigeon’s egg: mahāmuni.

children.text: sa tu caturmukho brahmā dvimukhastu varārgalaḥ
children.translated_text: When it has four faces it is brahmā; when two-faced, varārgala.
When six-faced it is kārtikeya; when five-faced, śaṃkara.
Mādhava is one-faced; vijayāśastradhāraṇa is another name.
For karañja: naktamāla, pūtīka, and cirabilvaka.
Karaja, ślīpadāri, prakīrya, and kalināśana are also names.
There are three varieties of it; among them, ṣaḍgranthā is hastivāruṇī.
For markaṭī: kṛtamāla, udakīrya, and prakīryaka.
For aṅgāravallī: śārṅgasthā, kāsaghnī, and karatālikā.
For rohītaka: rohitaka, rohī, and dāḍimapuṣpaka.
Rohaḍaka, sadāpuṣpa, rocanā, and plīharaktahā are also names.
For kaṭphala: somavalka, kaiṭarya, and gopabhadrikā.
Kumbhī, kumudikā, bhadrā, śrīparṇī, and bhadravatī are also names.
For dāḍima: kuṭṭima, kīravallabha, and phalaṣāṇḍava.
Karaka and dantabīja are also names; now, for oḍrapuṣpa: japā and javā.
For dhātakī: dhātupuṣpī, bahupuṣpī, and agnipuṣpikā.
Tāmraparṇī, subhikṣā, kuñjarā, and madyapāvanī are also names.

children.text: sallakyāṃ vallakī hrādā suvahā susravā rasā ||
children.translated_text: For sallakī: vallakī, hrādā, suvahā, susravā, and rasā.
Aśvamūrti, kundarukī, gajabhakṣyā, and maheraṇā are also names.
Gandhavīrā, gandhakārī, surabhi, and vanakarṇikā are also names.
For eraṇḍa: taruṇa, citra, dīrghadaṇḍa, and vyaḍambaka.
Pañcāṅgula, vardhamāna, āmaṇḍa, ruvaka, and ruvū are also names.
Vyāghrapuccha, vyāghratala, cañcu, and uttānapatraka are also names.
Gandharvahastaka, cañcu, ādaṇḍa, and hastiparṇaka are also names.

children.text: uruvūko hastikarṇaḥ śuklo raktaśca sa dvidhā
children.translated_text: Uruvūka and hastikarṇa are also names; it is of two kinds, white and red.
For kimpāka: mahākāla, kākarda, and kākamardaka.
For kampillaka: kāmpilla, raktāṅga, and raktacūrṇaka.
Candrāhvaya, rocanaka, karkaśāhva, and paṭodaya are also names.
Ketakacchadanīya, ambuprasādanaphala, and kata are also names.
For kārpāsī: samudrāntā, badarā, and tuṇḍikerī.

children.text: sā tu vanyā bharadvājī bhadrā candanabījikā
children.translated_text: That wild variety is bharadvājī, bhadrā, and candanabījikā.
For vandā: taruruhā, śauravarya, and darohiṇī.
Vṛkṣādanī, vṛkṣabhakṣyā, jayantī, and kāmapādapa are also names.
That which grows on the milk-tree is nandīvṛkṣa and jayadruma.
For āṭarūṣa: vṛṣa, vāsā, vāśikā, and vājidantaka.
Bhiṣaṅmātā, siṃhamukha, siṃhikā, and siṃhaparṇikā are also names.
For tumbara: sānuja, saura, saurabha, vanaja, and andhaka.
Tīkṣṇavalka, tīkṣṇaphala, tīkṣṇapattra, and mahāmuni are also names.
For kadalī: hastiviṣā, rambhā, mocā, and aṃśumatphalā.
Kāṣṭhīlā and vāraṇavuśā are names; kālīrasa is also given.
For tagara: kālānusārya, cakrākhya, madhura, and nṛpa.
For tūla: brahmacāru, brahmaṇya, and brahmakāṣṭhaka.

children.text: brahmaniṣṭhaṃ ca dāpaṃ ca kramukaṃ brahmacāri ca
children.translated_text: Brahmaniṣṭha, dāpa, kramuka, and brahmacārin are also names.
For muṣkaka: mokṣaka, ghaṇṭā, krandāla, mokṣa, and muñcaka.

children.text: pāṭalir golihaḥ kṣāraśreṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sitaśca saḥ
children.translated_text: Pāṭali, goliha, kṣāraśreṣṭha; it is both black and white.
For vaṃśa: yavaphala, veṇu, śataparvan, and tṛṇadhvaja.
Maskara, tvacisāra, tvaksāra, karmāra, and tejanā are also names.
For gāṅgerukī: viśvadeva, devāhva, svāṅga, and vedhukā.
Khaṇḍāriṣṭā, nāgabalā, and svarabandhanikā are also names.
For dāruharidrā: dārvī, pītā, and kaṭaṅkaṭerikā.
Pītadruma, pītadāru, pītana, and pītacandana are also names.
Parjanī, karkaṭakinī, kāleyaka, and pacampacā are also names.
For granthiparṇa: śliṣṭaparṇa, vikīrṇa, and śīrṇaromaka.

children.text: kukkuraṃ ca tathā gucchaṃ śukapuṣpaṃ śukacchadam ||
children.translated_text: Kukkura, guccha, śukapuṣpa, and śukacchada are also names.
Sthauṇeyaka, vahnicūḍā, and sugandhagranthikā are also names.
For spṛkkā: brāhmaṇī, paṅkamuṣṭikā, and śvanāvadhū.
Samudrāntā, marunmālā, nirmālyā, and devaputrikā are also names.
Laṅkātikā, koṭivarṣā, devī, and paṅkajamuṣṭikā are also names.
Gomī, svarṇalatā, indrāṇī, maranmālā, and latā laghu are also names.
For viḍaṅga: keralā, moghā, tandula, and kṛṣṇatandula.
Vellaka, kṛmihā, jantughātaka, and mṛgagāminī are also names.
For indrākṣa: ṛṣabha, vīra, śrīmān, and vṛṣabhanāmaka.
Dhūrdhura, gopati, śṛṅgī, bandhura, and pṛthivīpati are also names.

children.text: ṛdvau siddhiryugaṃ yogyaṃ rathāṅgaṃ maṅgalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: For ṛdvi: siddhi, yuga, yogya, rathāṅga, and maṅgala.
Ṛṣisṛṣṭasukha and lakṣmī are also names of vṛddhi.
For padmaka: mālaka, pīta, rakta, carusaru, and śyava.
Susabha, śītavīrya, pāṭala, and pītavarṇaka are also names.
For kaṅkuṣṭa: kākakuṣṭa, pulaka, and kākapālaka.
Recana, śodhana, hrāsa, viḍaṅga, and raṅgadāyaka are also names.
<s>Paro'para</s>, <s>para</s>, and also <s>parimaṇḍala</s> are further names for it.
For the date palm, the names are <s>tvagruja</s>, <s>piṇḍī</s>, <s>niḥśreṇi</s>, and <s>svādumastaka</s>.
For the palmyra palm, the names are <s>tala</s>, <s>lekhyapattra</s>, <s>tṛṇarāja</s>, and <s>dhvajadruma</s>.
For the coconut, the names are <s>rasaphala</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>kūrcakesara</s>.
<s>Dākṣiṇātya</s>, <s>dṛḍhaphala</s>, <s>nārikera</s>, and <s>latātaru</s> are also names for it.

children.text: pūge guvākaḥ kramukaḥ pūgī ca nīlavalkalaḥ
children.translated_text: For the areca nut, the names are <s>guvāka</s>, <s>kramuka</s>, <s>pūgī</s>, and <s>nīlavalkala</s>.
Its fruit is called <s>udvega</s>; in the case of the smooth one, the name is <s>cikkaṇa</s>.

children.text: tālyāṃ tu mṛtyupuṣpā syād ekapattraphalāpi ca
children.translated_text: For <s>tālī</s>, the names are <s>mṛtyupuṣpā</s> and also <s>ekapattraphalā</s>.
together with areca and coconut, are these grass-trees.
The white variety is <s>śvetasurasā</s>, <s>golomā</s>, and also <s>bhūtakeśī</s>.

children.text: sā tu śuklā bhūtakeśī satyanāmnī bahukṣamā

children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s> is the name for <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s>; it is also <s>natāṅgī</s> and <s>śiśirephalā</s>.

children.text: biḍālikā vṛkṣaparṇī mahāśvetā parā tu sā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>biḍālikā</s>, <s>vṛkṣaparṇī</s>, and <s>mahāśvetā</s>; the other variety is as follows:
For <s>nāgadantī</s>, the names are <s>hastidantī</s>, <s>vāruṇī</s>, and also <s>cirbhiṭī</s>.
For <s>māṣaparṇī</s>, the names are <s>sūryaparṇī</s>, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, and also <s>mahāsahā</s>.
For turmeric, the names are <s>varṇavatī</s>, <s>kāñcanī</s>, and <s>varavarṇinī</s>.
<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and <s>tīkṣṇagandha</s> are also names; the second kind is <s>vaṭapattraka</s>.

children.text: parṇāso bilvagandhaśca sa tu kṛṣṇaḥ sarālakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parṇāsa</s> and <s>bilvagandha</s> are names; that black variety is <s>sarālaka</s>.
Of it, the white variety is <s>gaurī</s>, <s>śakrapatnī</s>, <s>bhūtaghnī</s>, and <s>devadundubhi</s>.
